root.name: Bogo-Indian Defense: Wade-Smyslov Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Bb4+ 4. Bd2 a5

overview: After 4.Bd2 Black plays 4...a5, keeping the bishop on b4 so White cannot easily trade it, and White continues 5.g3 or 5.Nc3. Positions are solid and strategic: Black builds a solid set-up with ...O-O and ...d6 or ...d5 and White tries for a small space edge. If the bishop exchanges, White gets the bishop pair.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2 and play Nc3
Gain space with e4 or Qc2 if allowed

black_ideas.idea: Hold the bishop on b4 with ...a5 and play ...O-O, ...d6 or ...d5

typical_structures.structure: Queen's Gambit type centre with c4/d4 against e6/d5 or d6
Pins and bishop trades on c3

character.notes: Solid, positional play with little risk for Black.

structure.notes: The d4/c4 centre against e6 stays flexible.

character.reason: Black builds a hard-to-break set-up with few tactical risks.

structure.reason: The centre stays undecided with c4/d4 against e6.

approach.reason: A normal Indian-defence system for strong players.

level.reason: Positional ideas rather than long lines.

plans.reason: White often plays g3 and Bg2 against the Bogo-Indian.
